column1: # fuzz/accepted.tsv --- the grammar fuzz findings the owner has accepted.
# Adding a row is the owner's ruling, never a session's (CLAUDE.md). A
# finding a row names is reported "known, accepted (#N)" and does not fail
# a run; every other finding fails as before. A row names the issue that
# records the finding, the grammars it is reached through (comma-separated),
# the kinds it is seen as, the reproductions that identify it (paths
# relative to this directory, each dominated by one short repeated unit,
# which is the key), and the condition that removes the row. A row is keyed
# to the defect, not to the route a fuzzer took to it. fuzz/accepted/README.md
# says how a finding is matched and what the match cannot tell apart.
# The list is empty. #296 (markdown_inline's underscore and asterisk
# paragraphs, memory) and #301 (its nested image and link openers, hang)
# were accepted until a boundary on the parse itself stopped them in the
# editor; E7i's worker process does (each buffer's parse is killed at the
# deadline and stopped at its memory limit, tests/e7i_parse_containment_
# acceptance.rs), so their rows retired at E7i.5 and their reproductions
# moved to fuzz/regress/markdown/, which every arm of scripts/fuzz-grammars
# replays through the worker. The two rows are kept, as they stood, in
# tests/e7h_review2/accepted-296-301.tsv, which holds the matching itself
# under test.
